- **Agent-friendly design** — significant "glue" logic makes the raw Data360 API composable and safe for LLM tool use

---

## Installation & Version Pinning

Releases follow [Semantic Versioning](https://semver.org/); every release publishes a `vX.Y.Z` git tag plus a corresponding [GitHub Release](https://github.com/worldbank/data360-mcp/releases). Minor releases keep backward-compatible API contracts, so pin a major/minor to lock behavior.

Install the Python server from PyPI and pin a known-good release:

```bash
pip install data360-mcp==0.1.3
```

Roll back to an earlier verified release by installing any prior version listed on the [Releases page](https://github.com/worldbank/data360-mcp/releases):

```bash
pip install data360-mcp==<previous-version>
```

The `@data360/*` npm UI packages are published on every release under the same version number; pin them the same way:

```bash
npm install @data360/mcp-ui@X.Y.Z
```

See [DEVELOPMENT.md](DEVELOPMENT.md) for how releases are cut.

---

### Prerequisites

- **Python 3.11+**
- [uv](https://github.com/astral-sh/uv) (recommended) — or `pip`

### Installation

**With uv (recommended):**
```bash
git clone https://github.com/worldbank/data360-mcp.git
cd data360-mcp
uv sync
# LangChain / LangGraph client + examples + repo-root shim (data360_mcp_service.py):
uv sync --extra agent --group dev
```

**With pip:**
```bash
git clone https://github.com/worldbank/data360-mcp.git
cd data360-mcp
pip install -e .
```

### Configuration

Copy the example environment file and adjust as needed:

```bash
cp .env.example .env
```

| Variable | Description | Default |
|---|---|---|
| `DATA360_API_BASE_URL` | Base URL for the World Bank Data360 API | `https://data360api.worldbank.org` |
| `MCP_PORT` | Port for the MCP server | `8000` |
| `MCP_TRANSPORT` | Transport protocol (`http` or `sse`) | `http` |
| `MCP_CHARTS_API_URL` | Optional URL for an external chart rendering API | _(none)_ |
| `DATA360_READ_TIMEOUT` | Seconds to wait for a Data360 API response (connect/write/pool have their own knobs) | `8` |
| `DATA360_RETRY_MAX_ATTEMPTS` | Attempts for retry-safe requests (idempotent methods and read-only Data360 POSTs) | `3` |
| `DATA360_RETRY_BUDGET_SECONDS` | Wall-clock ceiling for retrying one request; set `<= DATA360_READ_TIMEOUT` to never retry a timeout | `16` |
| `DATA360_DEGRADATION_COOLDOWN_SECONDS` | How long a stale metadata snapshot is reused before the API is retried | `30` |
| `DATA360_BACKGROUND_READ_TIMEOUT` | Read timeout for background/bulk calls (dimension catalog, dataset catalogue, group hierarchy) on their own client + pool | `30` |
| `DATA360_BACKGROUND_INLINE_WAIT_SECONDS` | How long a user request may wait for the dimension catalog before serving raw codes (`0` never waits) | `2` |

### Run the Server

```bash
uv run poe serve
# Server starts at http://localhost:8000/mcp
```

Or with custom port/transport:
```bash
uv run poe serve --port 8021 --transport sse
# SSE endpoint: http://localhost:8021/sse
```

### Connect Your Agent

| Setting | Value |
|---|---|
| Transport | `http` (default) or `sse` |
| URL (http) | `http://localhost:8000/mcp` |
| URL (sse) | `http://localhost:8021/sse` |
| Docker / external | Replace `localhost` with `host.docker.internal` |

### Try the Demo

```bash
uv run scripts/llm_mcp_demo.py
# DEBUG mode:
DEBUG=true uv run scripts/llm_mcp_demo.py
```

**Minimal external agent (one-shot):** [examples/agents/langchain-minimal/README.md](examples/agents/langchain-minimal/README.md) — copy-paste `run_once.py` that loads `data360://system-prompt` and tools, then calls the model.

# data360-mcp-agent

**PyPI-oriented client library** for building LLM agents and LangGraph workflows against a **running** [Data360 MCP](https://github.com/worldbank/data360-mcp) server. This package does **not** embed the MCP server; you deploy or run the server separately and point this client at `DATA360_MCP_URL`.

## Install

```bash
pip install data360-mcp-agent
```

From a checkout of the `data360-mcp` monorepo (workspace):

```bash
uv sync --package data360-mcp-agent
# or
pip install -e packages/data360-mcp-agent
```

## Quick start

```python
import asyncio
from data360_mcp_agent import run_agent_query

async def main():
    out = await run_agent_query("GDP per capita for Kenya, last 10 years")
    print(out["answer"])

asyncio.run(main())
```

Environment (minimum):

| Variable | Description |
|----------|-------------|
| `DATA360_MCP_URL` | MCP HTTP URL, e.g. `http://127.0.0.1:8000/mcp` (match `MCP_PORT` / how you start the server) |

### Integration recipe (resources + MCP prompts)

The MCP server publishes **`data360://agent-recipe`** — composition order, named prompts (`gate_classifier`, `thematic_to_data`, `country_data`, …), and how they relate to this package.

- To append that doc into the agent’s **system stack** (longer context):
  `DATA360_AGENT_EXTRA_RESOURCES=data360://agent-recipe`

- **`fetch_mcp_prompt_messages(name, …)`** — fetch `gate_classifier`, `thematic_to_data`, etc., as LangChain messages when you want the **same wording** as the MCP server instead of only the gated node’s embedded prompts.

Python constant: **`AGENT_RECIPE_URI`** (`data360://agent-recipe`).

Additional environment variables:

| Variable | Description |
|----------|-------------|
| `DATA360_MCP_TRANSPORT` | Default `streamable_http` |
| `DATA360_MCP_STREAMABLE_TERMINATE_ON_CLOSE` | Optional `false` to skip MCP session DELETE on disconnect (rare) |
| `OPENAI_API_KEY` | If using default `ChatOpenAI` (or inject your own `llm`) |
| `DATA360_AGENT_LLM_STREAMING` | Optional `true` — default `ChatOpenAI` uses `streaming=True` for `astream_events` token chunks |

def _strip_data_row(row: dict[str, Any]) -> dict[str, Any]:
    """Strip boilerplate fields from a data row for LLM token savings.

    Keeps core fields (OBS_VALUE, TIME_PERIOD, REF_AREA, UNIT_MEASURE, claim_id)
    and conditionally includes disaggregation fields (SEX, AGE, URBANISATION,
    COMP_BREAKDOWN_1, COMP_BREAKDOWN_2) only when their value is non-trivial
    (i.e. not _T or _Z).

    Note: COMP_BREAKDOWN_3 is intentionally excluded -- it was observed as ``_Z``
    across all 16 surveyed databases and never carries data.

    Based on a 16-database survey documented in docs/payload_analysis.md.
    """
    filtered = {k: v for k, v in row.items() if k in _CORE_FIELDS}
    for field in _CONDITIONAL_FIELDS:
        val = row.get(field)
        if val and val not in _TRIVIAL_VALUES:
            filtered[field] = val
    return filtered

I read the data360-mcp repo at `.../scratchpad/repos/data360-mcp` without running or installing anything. In short: the Data360 REST API is public and needs no key, and the cheapest way to use it is to call two endpoints from a small httpx client in Django. Embedding this package or running the MCP server is not worth it on a 5-hour budget.

**1. Data360 REST API** (settings in `src/data360/config.py`, calls in `src/data360/api.py`)
- **Base URL:** `DATA360_API_BASE_URL=https://data360api.worldbank.org` (`.env.example`). `api_url` = `{base}/data360`.
- **Auth:** none. No API key or token is sent for Data360 calls. The only bearer token is for an optional charts store (`MCP_CHARTS_API_TOKEN`). The search payload limits results to public data with `"data_classification": ["public"]`.
- **Data** (`get_data`): `GET {base}/data360/data` with params `DATABASE_ID`, `INDICATOR`, `REF_AREA` (comma-separated, e.g. `KEN,TZA`), `timePeriodFrom`, `timePeriodTo`, `skip`, `top`. Optional dimension params: `SEX`, `AGE`, `URBANISATION`, `UNIT_MEASURE`, `COMP_BREAKDOWN_1/2`. The code notes the API uses `top`, not `$top`.
  - Response: `{"value": [rows], "@odata.count": n}`. Each row has `OBS_VALUE`, `TIME_PERIOD`, `REF_AREA`, `UNIT_MEASURE`, `UNIT_MULT`, `COMMENT_TS`, plus dimension columns.
  - Pagination: the code asks for `top=limit+1` to detect more rows, and `_fetch_all_pages` loops 100 rows per page up to 50 pages.
- **Search:** `POST {base}/data360/portal/v1/public_data360_search` with JSON `{"site":"data360","query_string":q,"types":["indicator"],"data_classification":["public"],"skip":0,"items_per_page":5}`, plus optional `economy_codes` and `database_names`.
  - Response: `count` or `@odata.count`, and items under `value`, `results` or `items`, each with `series_description{idno,name,database_id,...}`.
- **Metadata:** `POST {base}/data360/metadata` with body `{"query":"series_description/idno eq '<ID>'","select":"series_description/definition_long, ..."}`. Returns `value[0].series_description`.
- **Dimensions** (valid filter values): `POST {base}/data360/portal/v1/dimensions` with `{"database_id","indicator_id"}`. There is also an older `{api_url}/disaggregation` endpoint.
- **Other endpoints:**
  - Indicator list: `GET {base}/data360/indicators?datasetId=WB_WDI`
  - Dataset catalogue: `POST {base}/data360/searchv2` (OData `filter`, `select`, `skip`)
  - All codelists: `GET https://extdataportal.worldbank.org/api/data360/metadata/codelist`
  - Country groups: `https://fmr.worldbank.org/FMR/sdmx/v2/structure/hierarchy/WB/H_REF_AREA_GROUPS/{version}?format=sdmx-json`
- **Rate limits:** none are documented or enforced in the code. The client has 3s connect and 8s read timeouts, and retries up to 3 times on 429/502/503/504 within a 16s budget (`http_client.py`). `tests/test_rate_limits.py` is only a manual load test against Azure APIM.

**2. MCP tools** (`src/data360/mcp_server/tools.py`)
- **Lookup tools:**
  - `data360_search_indicators(query|queries|query_groups, required_country, limit=5, offset, result_layout, dedupe, database)`
  - `data360_search_datasets(query, limit, offset)`
  - `data360_get_metadata(database_id, indicator_id, select_fields, fetch_disaggregation, required_country)`
  - `data360_get_disaggregation(database_id, indicator_id, required_country)`
  - `data360_find_codelist_value(codelist_type, query, limit)` (country name to code)
  - `data360_list_indicators(database_id)`
  - `data360_expand_country_group(group_code)`
- **Data tools:**
  - `data360_get_data(database_id, indicator_id, country_code, disaggregation_filters, start_year, end_year, limit=50, offset, ref_area_filter="member_economies_only", year)` returns rows plus `has_more`, `next_offset` and `claim_id`.
  - `data360_get_data_api_url(...)` returns a ready-made data URL.
- **Analysis tools** (these paginate internally):
  - `data360_summarize_data(..., group_by)`
  - `data360_rank_countries(country_group|country_codes, year, order, top_n, rank_universe)`
  - `data360_compare_countries(country_codes, year, include_time_series, ...)`
- **Chart tools:**
  - `data360_get_viz_spec(..., chart_type, relevant_fields, custom_constraints, chart_title, series_labels, strategy_override)`
  - `data360_get_multi_indicator_viz_spec(indicator_ids=[{database_id, indicator_id}], ...)`
  - `data360_get_supported_chart_types()`
  - `data360_interactive_choices(prompt, options, title)`
- **Resources** (`resources.py`): `data360://system-prompt`, `data360://agent-recipe`, `data360://context`, `data360://databases`, `data360://codelists`, `data360://metadata-fields`, `data360://data-filters`, `data360://data-schema`, `data360://search-usage`, `data360://k360-narrative-style`, `data360://viz/chart-grammar`, plus `ui://` HTML renderers.
- **Prompts** (`prompts.py`): `gate_classifier`, `thematic_to_data`, `indicator_search`, `indicator_details`, `country_data`, `k360_research_compiler`, `k360_narrative`.
- **System prompt grounding rules:**
  - The model must call tools for any data value and must not guess.
  - Fixed order: search, then resolve codes, then check availability, then fetch data.
  - Pick one best indicator and state "Selected Indicator: [ID] — [Name]" and why.
  - Ask the user when a series is ambiguous (real vs nominal, KD vs CD units).
  - Default time range is the last 5 years.
  - Strip `()` and `$` from search queries.
- **Narrative rules:** answers use Data / Analysis / Note / Sources sections, always give units and years, may tag numbers with `<claim id>`, and say clearly when data is missing.

**3. Python install and usage**
- PyPI package `data360-mcp`. The README pins `==0.1.3` but `pyproject.toml` says `0.1.2`.
- Run with `python -m data360.mcp_server -t stdio|streamable-http -p 8021`, or `uvicorn data360.server:app` (HTTP at `/mcp`).
- Importing `data360.api.get_data` directly from Django is technically possible, but I don't recommend it:
  - The functions are async and depend on module-level settings (`DATA360_API_BASE_URL` is required).
  - The dependencies are heavy: fastmcp, pandas 3, scikit-learn, Azure telemetry, and a git-pinned `draco` fork.
- `packages/data360-mcp-agent` is a LangChain/LangGraph client (with `langchain-openai`) for an MCP server that is already running (`DATA360_MCP_URL`). It is not useful for a Django backend.

**4. Security patterns worth copying**
- `validation.py`: country codes are checked against an allowlist regex `[A-Z0-9]{1,4}` and bad tokens are dropped.
- `security_validator.py`:
  - Regex blocklist for prompt injection ("ignore previous instructions", "you are now a", "then call", dunder names).
  - Search terms must be 3 to 100 characters; wildcard-only queries are rejected.
  - Tool-name allowlist (`data360_*` only).
  - `sanitize_string` truncates and strips null bytes.
- `server.py` `SecurityValidationMiddleware` returns 403 with the message passed through `html.escape`.
- `response_safety.py` sets `X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff`; templates use Jinja autoescape and `|tojson` for values inside scripts.
- To avoid leaking internals, 500 responses return a generic message and details are logged server-side (`tests/test_information_leakage.py`).
- Logs pass user values through `repr()` to block log injection, and an audit log records a SHA-256 hash of each request.
- Weak points not to copy:
  - CORS is `allow_origins=["*"]`, and host/origin defaults to `["*"]` (`_server_definition.py`).
  - There is no rate limiting in the app.
  - `get_metadata` pastes `indicator_id` straight into the OData filter string. In our app, validate IDs with `^[A-Z0-9_]+$`.

**5. Visualization**
- `viz_config.py` defines 14 chart types in `ChartStrategy`, chosen by `select_strategy()` running through a list of rule classes.
- Routing for one indicator:
  - Several years and up to 8 countries: line.
  - One year and up to 8 countries: horizontal bar.
  - One year and more than 8 countries: strip chart.
  - A breakdown such as sex or age: small multiples.
- Routing for two indicators: scatter for one year, connected scatter across years.
- Specs are Vega-Lite with a World Bank theme (`wb_altair_config`, `inject_wb_config`).
- These routing thresholds are easy to copy as plain if/else logic; the code itself is heavy.

**6. IDs and country codes**
- Indicator ID = `{DATABASE_ID}_{WDI code with dots replaced by _}`, e.g. `WB_WDI_SP_POP_TOTL`, `WB_WDI_NY_GDP_PCAP_KD`, `WB_WDI_SP_DYN_LE00_IN`. The database ID is `WB_WDI`.
- Scorecard `EG_ELC_ACCS_ZS` should therefore map to `WB_WDI_EG_ELC_ACCS_ZS`. That follows from the naming pattern; I haven't confirmed that indicator exists.
- `REF_AREA` uses ISO3 codes (`KEN`) and World Bank aggregate codes (`SSF`, `LIC`, `SAS`). There is no ISO2 support, so we need our own ISO2-to-ISO3 table (e.g. `pycountry`).

**7. License**
- MIT (© 2025 The World Bank Group) plus the World Bank IGO Rider (`LICENSE`, `WB-IGO-RIDER.md`). The `.github` attribution header said Apache-2.0, but the LICENSE file is MIT.
- The rider is procedural only: it preserves World Bank immunities and sets mediation then arbitration for disputes, with no support obligation. It adds no limits on reuse; keep the copyright notice.

**8. Recommendation**
Write a small `data360.py` service in Django using `httpx` or `requests`:
- `fetch_series(indicator_id, iso3_list, start, end)` calls `GET https://data360api.worldbank.org/data360/data` with `DATABASE_ID=WB_WDI`, `INDICATOR`, `REF_AREA`, `timePeriodFrom`, `timePeriodTo`, `top=1000`. Loop on `skip` until fewer than `top` rows come back.
- Keep a fixed allowlist of about 10 WDI indicators (population, GDP, GDP per capita, life expectancy, electricity access, and so on) rather than letting the LLM search freely.
- Validate IDs with `^[A-Z0-9_]+$` and countries against the ISO3 regex or allowlist.
- Set a 3s connect / 8s read timeout and cache results in Django's cache for about 24 hours (or load nightly into a model).
- Convert Scorecard ISO2 codes to ISO3 when joining.
- Send the LLM only rows we fetched ourselves, tagged with source and year (the `claim_id` idea), and reuse the system prompt's grounding and narrative rules.
- Put Django's `html.escape` or autoescape on all output, use generic error messages, add `nosniff`, and rate-limit per IP (e.g. `django-ratelimit`).

This avoids the MCP layer entirely while keeping the same grounding guarantees. Use the search endpoint only if we need to discover indicators at runtime.

- Logs pass user values through `repr()` to block log injection, and an audit log records a SHA-256 hash of each request.
- Weak points not to copy:
  - CORS is `allow_origins=["*"]`, and host/origin defaults to `["*"]` (`_server_definition.py`).
  - There is no rate limiting in the app.
  - `get_metadata` pastes `indicator_id` straight into the OData filter string. In our app, validate IDs with `^[A-Z0-9_]+$`.

**5. Visualization**
- `viz_config.py` defines 14 chart types in `ChartStrategy`, chosen by `select_strategy()` running through a list of rule classes.
- Routing for one indicator:
  - Several years and up to 8 countries: line.
  - One year and up to 8 countries: horizontal bar.
  - One year and more than 8 countries: strip chart.
  - A breakdown such as sex or age: small multiples.
- Routing for two indicators: scatter for one year, connected scatter across years.
- Specs are Vega-Lite with a World Bank theme (`wb_altair_config`, `inject_wb_config`).
- These routing thresholds are easy to copy as plain if/else logic; the code itself is heavy.

**6. IDs and country codes**
- Indicator ID = `{DATABASE_ID}_{WDI code with dots replaced by _}`, e.g. `WB_WDI_SP_POP_TOTL`, `WB_WDI_NY_GDP_PCAP_KD`, `WB_WDI_SP_DYN_LE00_IN`. The database ID is `WB_WDI`.
- Scorecard `EG_ELC_ACCS_ZS` should therefore map to `WB_WDI_EG_ELC_ACCS_ZS`. That follows from the naming pattern; I haven't confirmed that indicator exists.
- `REF_AREA` uses ISO3 codes (`KEN`) and World Bank aggregate codes (`SSF`, `LIC`, `SAS`). There is no ISO2 support, so we need our own ISO2-to-ISO3 table (e.g. `pycountry`).

**8. Recommendation**
Write a small `data360.py` service in Django using `httpx` or `requests`:
- `fetch_series(indicator_id, iso3_list, start, end)` calls `GET https://data360api.worldbank.org/data360/data` with `DATABASE_ID=WB_WDI`, `INDICATOR`, `REF_AREA`, `timePeriodFrom`, `timePeriodTo`, `top=1000`. Loop on `skip` until fewer than `top` rows come back.
- Keep a fixed allowlist of about 10 WDI indicators (population, GDP, GDP per capita, life expectancy, electricity access, and so on) rather than letting the LLM search freely.
- Validate IDs with `^[A-Z0-9_]+$` and countries against the ISO3 regex or allowlist.
- Set a 3s connect / 8s read timeout and cache results in Django's cache for about 24 hours (or load nightly into a model).
- Convert Scorecard ISO2 codes to ISO3 when joining.
- Send the LLM only rows we fetched ourselves, tagged with source and year (the `claim_id` idea), and reuse the system prompt's grounding and narrative rules.
- Put Django's `html.escape` or autoescape on all output, use generic error messages, add `nosniff`, and rate-limit per IP (e.g. `django-ratelimit`).

This avoids the MCP layer entirely while keeping the same grounding guarantees. Use the search endpoint only if we need to discover indicators at runtime.
